pubmed._query_note:
Validated 2026-08-24 against a live Q count of 329,274; live count at write time 329,278.

Ten-year window (years_back=10). This matches the shipped NSCLC corpus, which was built at pubmed_days_back=3650. NSCLC's JSON records years_back=null, but that path has never run: the NSCLC corpus came from the DB therapeutic_area_ingestion_config row in May 2026, not from this JSON. Ten years is the product decision; null is an untested value.

MeSH tree verified by count arithmetic, not by diagram. Anus Neoplasms is 100% inside Rectal Neoplasms, Appendiceal is 100% inside Cecal, and Cecal sits OUTSIDE the Colorectal branch entirely. Hence NoExp on Colorectal, Rectal and Cecal; Colonic is safe to explode (wholly inside Colorectal).

The Cecal[Mesh:NoExp] clause earns 1,529 unique PMIDs -- 58% of that branch is unreachable without it. Do not remove.

The anchored CRC[tiab] clause adds only 260 unique papers. Its justification is SUPPRESSION, not retrieval: unanchoring it admits 3,298 papers where "CRC" appears with no colorectal/colon/rectal token. 12.7:1 noise-to-signal. Do not simplify it away on low unique yield.

Scope excludes anal, appendiceal, small bowel, GIST, GI NETs, and screening/surveillance. Screening is excluded via a [majr] NOT block that sheds 24,597 papers; a 25-title sample of the unclassified remainder found 21/25 out of scope and no hidden treatment category. Known cost: ~800 treatment-adjacent papers, ~0.24% of the corpus.

Contamination probes: anal 0.48%, appendiceal 0.19%, gastric 2.22%, pancreatic 1.04%, lung 3.22%. Two-corpus overlap with the live NSCLC query is 3,397 papers, 1% of Q.

Interior precision NOT measured pre-ingest. Sample 200 titles in SQL after ingestion.
